rationale: A defensible leg-swap that directly diagnoses why the runway ratio had a strong alpha but a perverse FMB slope, though it is the fifth entry in the MIN-conjunction family and risks incremental rather than mechanistic gain, and the "profitability leg held constant" claim is only a clean test if the runway rank's coverage (0.106) doesn't itself drive the difference.

This is mechanical stacking of two already-archived conjunctions (broad liquidity leg + rollover leg) onto the same profitability leg with no new economic content, and deeper MIN nesting makes the score an order statistic of four correlated ranks, which compresses dispersion and destabilizes the long portfolio rather than sharpening the mechanism.

IND_RANK of an already-computed within-industry score is a strictly monotone transform, so the sorted portfolios and hence ls_alpha/ls_talpha/ls_sharpe are unchanged by construction and only the FMB slope moves as a pure rescaling artifact — this is a cosmetic variant of the archived best signal, not a testable economic hypothesis.

The coverage motivation is legitimate and the sign/expression are internally consistent, but the accrual leg is textbook Sloan (1996) balance-sheet accruals and the interaction itself is already archived, and critically Compustat wcap = act − lct so DELTA(wcap) is mechanically linked to the wcap/lct illiquidity leg, contaminating the interaction with a spurious own-variable dependence (and importing cash and short-term-debt changes into the "accrual").

target_name: Current Assets Per Dollar Of Operating Costs
rationale: act/(cogs+xsga) is essentially days-of-working-capital, i.e. the inverse of current-asset turnover, so a positive expected sign runs against both the Novy-Marx turnover decomposition and the net-operating-assets/working-capital-bloat literature, which say bloated current assets predict *lower* returns — the hypothesis asserts resilience where the established reading is inefficiency.

target_name: Rising Overhead On A Short Runway
rationale: The burn-acceleration interaction is genuinely distinct from the archive's level-based coverage ratios and the expression's direction matches the negative expected sign, but SG&A growth is strongly correlated with sales and asset growth, so absent scaling by revenue growth the short leg may simply rediscover the asset-growth/investment anomaly.
